candidates.decision_relevance: Repeated analyses rely on point-in-time top-100 breadth proxies whose membership changes between captures; a comparable history would help distinguish persistent participation changes from composition effects when assessing rotation or deterioration.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily Director outputs from 2026-10-09 through 2026-10-12 note changing point-in-time membership hashes and unconfirmed canonical breadth; weekly reviews also cite unavailable breadth paths and methodology.
candidates.missing_history_problem: Historical breadth counts are reported, but constituent-level membership and advancer status aligned across captures are not supplied. Without them, apparent breadth changes may reflect universe turnover rather than persistent participation.

candidates.decision_relevance: Flow direction and persistence are repeatedly used as counterevidence to or support for transmission and deterioration, but the available settled rows are isolated or mixed sessions.
candidates.evidence_reference: Daily outputs commonly cite only the latest settled session and explicitly leave intervening sessions missing; weekly reviews describe divergent ETF flows without directional sequence detail.
candidates.metric_name: Dated settled BTC and ETH ETF net-flow history
candidates.missing_history_problem: The supplied records do not provide a continuous dated sequence sufficient to establish whether flows persisted, reversed, or were concentrated in isolated sessions.

candidates.decision_relevance: The analyses repeatedly identify hindsight and sequence risks and report zero eligible prospective typed warning outcomes. Timestamped warning records linked to subsequent eligible price paths would make premature-versus-late warning assessments empirically inspectable.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly reviews W35-W40 and multiple daily outputs state that warning timestamps, subsequent eligible outcomes, or matured typed warning rows are absent or zero.
candidates.metric_name: Timestamped warning episodes with eligible subsequent outcome paths
candidates.missing_history_problem: Without preserved warning timestamps and episode-linked subsequent observations, the record cannot distinguish a warning that preceded deterioration from one assigned retrospectively, or quantify post-warning upside and drawdown descriptively.

candidates.decision_relevance: Several reviews report range candidates but lack their bounds, issuance times, realized metric paths, and baseline comparisons; preserving these would permit direct audit of range containment versus precision without using completed outcomes as decision-time evidence.
candidates.evidence_reference: Weekly W34-W40 reviews repeatedly report candidate counts while stating candidate definitions, bounds, issue timestamps, or realized candidate-linked outcomes are unavailable.
candidates.metric_name: Frozen forecast-candidate specifications and linked realized paths
candidates.missing_history_problem: Candidate counts alone do not allow reconstruction of what was forecast when, whether the specified horizon and bounds were evaluated as issued, or whether apparent containment was unusually informative.
